 1                              I.    INTRODUCTION

 2   Q.   Please state your name, current position, and business address.

 3   A.   My name is Adrian J. Rodriguez. I am the President of Southwestern Public

 4        Service Company, a New Mexico corporation (“SPS”), a wholly-owned electric

 5        utility subsidiary of Xcel Energy Inc. (“Xcel Energy”). My business address is 790

 6        South Buchanan Street, Amarillo, Texas 79101. My qualifications are provided in

 7        Attachment AJR-1.

 8   Q.   How long have you worked for SPS and Xcel Energy?

 9   A.   I have worked for SPS since June 2022.

10   Q.   On whose behalf are you testifying in this proceeding?

11   A.   I am testifying on behalf of SPS.

12   Q.   What is the purpose of your testimony in this proceeding?

13   A.   My testimony provides an overview of SPS, its operations, and its commitment to

14        providing our customers the safe, clean, reliable, and resilient energy services they

15        want and value at a competitive price. I also introduce SPS’s rate filing application,

16        including SPS’s requested authorized return on equity (“ROE”) and capital

17        structure, the benefits to SPS customers of the resource additions and system


                                                1
                                  Case No. 25-00___-UT
                                   Direct Testimony
                                           of
                                  Adrian J. Rodriguez

 1   upgrades SPS is making, costs associated with wildfire mitigation, and other

 2   investments SPS is making to modernize its grid. I conclude by discussing how a

 3   favorable outcome in this case will allow SPS to not only provide “adequate,

 4   efficient, and reasonable service,” 1 consistent with the Public Utility Act, but to go

 5   beyond and advance our strategic objectives of delivering excellent service, making

 6   customer interactions easier, guiding our customers and communities with

 7   expertise, and leading the clean energy transition.

 8             SPS is investing in a changing energy landscape and modernizing the grid

 9   to provide a safe, reliable, sustainable, and reasonable essential service to its New

10   Mexico customers. In particular, to meet our core mission and statutory obligations,

11   SPS is investing in a mix of new generation resources and associated transmission

12   network upgrades, while taking steps to keep costs as low as possible for New

13   Mexico customers and meeting its clean energy commitments. SPS is adding

14   renewable resources while also prioritizing the addition of flexible dispatchable

15   generation, including battery storage, to ensure reliability as it continues to

16   transition its generation fleet in the years to come, consistent with New Mexico’s



     1
         NMSA (2024) § 62-8-2.
                                           2
                                 Case No. 25-00___-UT
                                  Direct Testimony
                                          of
                                 Adrian J. Rodriguez

1    Energy Transition Act (“ETA”). Further, SPS returns the value of federal tax

2    credits generated by the renewable resources it owns to our customers. SPS is also

3    making capital investments in the reliability and resiliency of its existing

4    transmission and distribution infrastructure through system-wide planning and

5    spending on wildfire mitigation as described in our Wildfire Mitigation Plan. SPS

6    recognizes the need to improve the capacity of its systems in order to meet the

7    increasing electrification of its service territory, from the oil fields to the increase

 8   of electric heating and electric vehicles for our residential customers.

 9           SPS is committed to continuing to participate in the clean energy transition

10   in a manner that does not compromise reliability. Flexible, dispatchable resources

11   will have to continue to play a role in SPS’s generation mix as it moves toward a

12   lower carbon future. SPS will continue to run its remaining fossil units in a safe,

13   reliable, and economical manner, and SPS is pursuing new natural gas-fired

14   generation where conditions warrant it. For instance, SPS is currently seeking

15   approval for the Gaines County gas-fired facility. If the New Mexico Public

16   Regulation Commission (“Commission”) issues SPS a CCN to construct and

17   operate that project, a portion of the project has been shown to meet the definition

18   of a zero-carbon resource in New Mexico’s Renewable Energy Act § 62-16-3(K).

                                            3
                                 Case No. 25-00___-UT
                                  Direct Testimony
                                          of
                                 Adrian J. Rodriguez

 1   Although the Gaines County facility is not included in this case, it is illustrative of

 2   SPS’s efforts to identify resources that are consistent with the clean energy

 3   transition and the requirements in the ETA, while prioritizing the reliability of the

 4   system.

 5          In order to continue to reliably and affordably transition its generation

 6   resources, SPS must incorporate into its base rate revenue timely recovery of its

7    investments in infrastructure and expenses required to support our service territory,

8    to promote economic development, and to maintain and improve our operations, as

9    well as be provided an opportunity to earn a fair return on its investments.

10          Our mission to provide safe, clean, and reliable energy services at the lowest

11   cost possible, and our commitment to moving New Mexico toward a lower carbon

12   future, drive our actions at SPS. Our corporate mission translates into a workforce

13   that shares a deep sense of duty to our communities and other stakeholders. I look

14   forward to working with the Commission and all stakeholders to ensure that the

15   new rates established for SPS continue to allow us to make necessary investments

16   in our system to safely and reliably serve its customers, provide clean cost-effective

2   to provide the clean and reliable energy our customers and the policymakers of this

3   State expect.

 1                         II.   COMPANY DESCRIPTION

 2   Q.   Can you provide a general description of SPS’s electric operations?

 3   A.   Yes. SPS is a New Mexico corporation and a wholly-owned electric utility

 4        subsidiary of Xcel Energy. SPS’s total company service territory encompasses a

 5        52,000-square-mile area in eastern and southeastern New Mexico, the Texas

 6        Panhandle, and the Texas South Plains. SPS’s primary business as an electric utility

 7        is generating, transmitting, distributing, and selling electric energy. SPS provides

 8        retail electric services in New Mexico and Texas and serves approximately 415,000

 9        customers and 96 communities in its two-state system. SPS serves approximately

10        132,200 customers and 16 communities in New Mexico. SPS’s electric system is

11        composed of approximately 42 power plant generating units, including 2,611

12        megawatts (“MW”) of renewable energy projects. Eleven of SPS’s power plant

13        generating units are located in New Mexico. SPS has more than 24,000 miles of

14        overhead and underground transmission and distribution lines and 479 substations

15        in its two-state system, including 7,213 miles of transmission and distribution lines

16        and 137 substations in New Mexico. SPS is a member of the Southwest Power

17        Pool, Inc. Regional Transmission Organization and is synchronously connected to

18        the Eastern Interconnection. SPS is thus in a different resource position than other

                                               6
                               Case No. 25-00___-UT
                                Direct Testimony
                                        of
                               Adrian J. Rodriguez

1   New Mexico utilities that are members of the Western Electricity Coordinating

2   Council (as well as other Texas utilities that are members of the Electric Reliability

3   Council of Texas). A map of the SPS service territory is included as Attachment

4   AJR-2 to my testimony and is represented as Figure ARJ-1 below.

5                                  Figure ARJ-1

                                  Case No. 25-00___-UT

                                  Adrian J. Rodriguez

4   Q.   What is the customer load on SPS’s system?

5   A.   SPS’s New Mexico service territory is growing rapidly, and we must keep up with


                                            8
                                Case No. 25-00___-UT
                                 Direct Testimony
                                         of
                                Adrian J. Rodriguez

1    that growth. Unlike many utilities, the load on SPS’s system is predominantly

2    commercial and industrial (“C&I”). While residential customers comprise 79% of

3    SPS’s total customer count, they account for only 13% of the load on the SPS

4    system. In New Mexico, residential customers represent 15% of the system load.

5    Notwithstanding their comparably small size of SPS’s overall load, our residential

6    customers benefit from a resilient electric system that continues to keep the lights

7    on in their homes, in the schools where they send their children, in the retail and

8    grocery stores where they shop, and at their places of work, whether it is a small

9    commercial organization, government office, or large C&I company. Along with

10   our residential customers, SPS’s large C&I customers rightfully expect timely,

11   necessary, and reliable capital investment to continue to provide reliable electric

12   service to support their businesses. The predominance of C&I customers in SPS’s

13   service territory means we must always be prepared to make substantial

14   investments promptly in order to address the service needs of our commercial and

15   industrial customers, which can involve significant incremental load additions. In

16   responding promptly to our customers’ needs, we also support the economy of New

17   Mexico. Our ability to keep the energy flowing to our commercial customers can

18   impact their own employees and customers; thereby, impacting other major sectors

                                          9
                               Case No. 25-00___-UT
                                Direct Testimony
                                        of
                               Adrian J. Rodriguez

1   of the state’s economy. SPS has an obligation to serve, and SPS’s ability to respond

2   to the needs of commercial and residential customers is in the State’s best interest.




                                         10
                                     Case No. 25-00___-UT
                                      Direct Testimony
                                              of
                                     Adrian J. Rodriguez

 1                   III.    OVERVIEW OF SPS’S APPLICATION

 2   Q.   Why is SPS filing this case?

 3   A.   The outcome of this rate case will be important not only for SPS, but also for our

 4        customers, communities, and employees as well as the State of New Mexico’s clean

 5        energy future. Some of the most notable aspects of the case from the Company and

 6        customer perspective include:

 7           •   SPS’s generation additions into 2027, including new resources added to
 8               SPS’s fleet since our last rate case. Those resources include Plant X Solar,
 9               Cunningham 1 Solar, Cunningham 2 Solar, and the Cunningham Battery
10               Energy Storage System (“BESS”), as well as BESS resources identified
11               through a request for proposals (“RFP”) issued in 2024, for which SPS is
12               currently seeking Commission approval.
13           •   Investment in wildfire mitigation in SPS’s service territory, including
14               investments reflected in SPS’s Wildfire Mitigation Plan, which carries
15               increased capital and operations and maintenance expenses (“O&M”).
16           •   Grid investments that have and will continue to ensure our transmission and
17               distribution networks will be more resilient, ready to support the evolving
18               needs of our customers, and meet our clean energy goals, consistent with
19               the New Mexico ETA.
20           •   SPS’s proposal to extend the retirement dates for all of its facilities by three
21               months from December 31 of a given year to March 31 of the following
22               year, in order to better align with SPS’s requirement as a Load Serving
23               Entity within the Southwest Power Pool to meet seasonal Planning Reserve
24               Margins.
25           •   SPS’s request for resolution of its requested ratemaking treatment in several
26               recent cases, which treatment we now seek to resolve through this
27               proceeding. Those open decisions include requests for treatment of

                                               11
                                    Case No. 25-00___-UT
                                     Direct Testimony
                                             of
                                    Adrian J. Rodriguez

 1               investment tax credits, creation of a deferred tax asset for tax credits that
 2               accrue prior to SPS’s ability to use or transfer the credits, request for
 3               recovery of costs associated with the Time of Use (“TOU”) Fuel Pilot, and
 4               associated tariff changes.
 5           •   SPS’s request for approval of its proposed Energy Assistance Program.
 6           •   SPS’s request for cost recovery of increased dismantling costs and to set
 7               depreciation schedules for new generation assets that will be added to the
 8               system by November 2027.
 9           •   SPS’s efforts to address industry-wide inflation and price increase issues,
10               as well as certain labor issues SPS is experiencing, including a new
11               Collective Bargaining Agreement and need to increase headcount to
12               continue meeting our customers’ needs while providing a safe, well-paying
13               employment.

14           Constructive regulatory decisions in these areas will help provide price

15        certainty to our customers, while helping to ensure SPS has a sound financial

16        foundation to serve our communities and continue to reliably and affordably meet

17        our clean energy transition goals and requirements.


18   Q.   Are there notable activities SPS is currently engaged in that are not included

19        in this case?

20   A.   Yes. SPS is seeking to add almost 5,000 MW of capacity through a fleet of new

21        resources that were identified through its 2024 RFP, and additional resources that

22        remain to be identified. A limited number of these resources will reach commercial


                                              12
                                             Case No. 25-00___-UT
                                              Direct Testimony
                                                      of
                                             Adrian J. Rodriguez

 1           operation by the end of the future test year—namely the Plant X BESS, for which

 2           SPS is seeking cost recovery, and six long-term purchased power agreements

 3           (“LTPPAs”), for which SPS seeks to recover capacity costs—as SPS witnesses Zoë

 4           E. Lees and Justin L. Gable describe in further detail. 2 A majority of those resources

 5           will not, however, become used and useful for SPS and its customers until after the

 6           end of the future test year. Therefore, those resources will be presented in a later

 7           case. I and other witnesses discuss the portfolio of resources, however, to advise

 8           the Commission, potential intervenors, and the public of the significant investments

 9           SPS is making in the future of its system, as these necessary investments will have

10           a future impact on SPS’s rates.

11   Q.      How did SPS construct this case?

12   A.      SPS’s rate filing is comprised of a Base Period, 3 Adjusted Base Period, 4 Linkage

 2            3(P), and 62-6-14(D) of the Public Utility Act and Rule 17.1.3 of the New Mexico

 3            Administrative Code (the “Future Test Year Rule”). As Ms. Lees discusses in her

 4            direct testimony, SPS has fully explained and justified its Future Test Year costs,

 5            has broken down costs by cost center and elements of cost on a jurisdictional basis,

 6            and has explained material changes between the Adjusted Base Period and Future

13            reflects an equity ratio of 56%, an authorized ROE of 10.5%, and a cost of debt of

 1        support these requests in their respective direct testimonies.

 2   Q.   What would the impact be if SPS were unable to recover its costs?

 3   A.   SPS employees are proud to provide safe and reliable energy service to our

 4        customers, enhance the energy service our customers expect, and continue to lead

 5        the energy transition, which is consistent with the policy goals of this State as

 6        reflected in the New Mexico ETA. SPS’s request in this case will promote financial

 7        stability and allow SPS to continue to provide that service and achieve New

 8        Mexico’s public policy objectives. In contrast, limited financial resources can

 9        impact service quality and compromise a company’s ability to meet required

10        service and State objectives. Without full consideration of the details and tools

11        presented in this case, SPS will not possess the financial strength to concurrently

12        meet its energy transition goals consistent with the New Mexico ETA while

13        providing safe and reliable core utility services to customers. We are honored to

14        serve our customers in New Mexico and excited to continue to lead the energy

15        transition while working to keep the electricity flowing and to keep bills as low as

16        possible. For SPS to be successful in these endeavors, the support requested in this

17        case is key.



                                               15
                                      Case No. 25-00___-UT
                                       Direct Testimony
                                               of
                                      Adrian J. Rodriguez

 1   Q.   How can the Commission support SPS’s ability to attract the capital

 2        investment that is necessary for continued safety and reliability and supportive

 3        of economic growth?

 4   A.   The Commission’s decisions with respect to rate of return and capital structure will

 5        have a significant impact on SPS’s ability to meet its investment goals in the future.

 6        A constructive outcome in this proceeding will enable SPS to continue providing

 7        reliable service, as required by the New Mexico Public Utility Act, and to move

 8        toward a lower-carbon future, consistent with the New Mexico ETA. Mr. Wehner

 9        and Ms. Bulkley explain that rating agencies are keenly aware of the challenges

10        that utilities face when funding large capital investment projects, as well as other

11        aspects of the utility business that impact cash flows. Supportive decisions

12        approving SPS’s requested equity ratio, ROE, and capital structure from regulators

13        are viewed positively by the ratings agencies, which, in turn, provide the ratings by

14        which utilities ultimately finance necessary capital investment. To put it differently,

15        better ratings result in better financing opportunities, rates, and terms for utilities,

16        which ultimately benefit customers through a lower cost of debt. The Commission’s

17        ultimate approval of the settlement agreement in our last base rate case was viewed

18        as constructive; however, as discussed by Mr. Wehner, rating agencies are looking

                                                16
                                      Case No. 25-00___-UT
                                       Direct Testimony
                                               of
                                      Adrian J. Rodriguez

 1        to see consistent constructive outcomes in New Mexico in order to improve their

 2        risk profile of the regulatory environment.

 3   Q.   Will a constructive regulatory result in this case benefit customers and the

 4        State of New Mexico?

 5   A.   Absolutely. SPS is committed to providing the electricity that our region needs to

 6        remain strong and vibrant. Our regional economy cannot grow without a reliable

 7        and robust electric grid, and the construction of that grid is a large part of what is

 8        driving the need for this rate case. We want to help the communities and businesses

 9        in our service territory grow, but the expansion of our facilities requires that we

10        recover our costs and earn a reasonable return on our investment. Today’s grid

11        must evolve and be upgraded to support both the increased electricity demand and

12        the clean energy transition that are before us. This case represents an opportunity

13        for SPS and the Commission to build a constructive regulatory relationship that

14        improves investor opinion and ensures that SPS’s generation resources and

15        transmission and distribution systems can meet growth requirements while

16        remaining safe, resilient, and reliable.




                                                17
                                       Case No. 25-00___-UT
                                        Direct Testimony
                                                of
                                       Adrian J. Rodriguez

 1        IV.    NEW MEXICO PROVIDES CONSTRUCTIVE REGULATORY
 2                             OUTCOMES

 3   Q.    What is the purpose of this section of your direct testimony?

 4   A.    In this section of my direct testimony, I explain how a constructive outcome in this

 5         case will, if granted, allow SPS to continue advancing our strategic priorities by

 6         investing in a changing energy landscape and modernizing the grid to provide safe,

 7         reliable, sustainable, and reasonable essential service.

 8         A.     Delivering Excellent Service
 9   Q.    Please describe SPS’s goals for delivering excellent service.

10   A.    We are working diligently to ensure that our customers always have energy when

11         they need it most. SPS is proud of the reliability of our service, and we continue to

12         strive to raise the bar on resilience, reliability, safety, and customers’ costs. We are

13         focused on delivering on our promise to meet a growing energy demand and protect

14         our existing systems from severe weather events like wildfire, while keeping costs

15         as low as possible. We do this by making significant investments in infrastructure,

16         including the new energy sources, more resilient power networks, and other

17         projects described in this application.




                                                 18
                                      Case No. 25-00___-UT
                                       Direct Testimony
                                               of
                                      Adrian J. Rodriguez

 1   Q.   How is SPS working to enhance the reliability and resilience of its system?

 2   A.   SPS has been making, and will continue to make, significant investments to ensure

 3        that our New Mexico customers receive the reliable electric service they need and

4         expect. As Ms. Lees and others discuss, SPS is actively investing in planning and

5         upgrading its electrical system to support its transitioning generation fleet. Not only

6         must the grid be ready as New Mexico utilities approach the next series of clean

 7        energy milestones under the New Mexico ETA, but SPS must be in a strong

 8        financial position to ensure the clean energy transition continues in a reliable and

 9        cost-effective manner for customers.

10               SPS is also making investments to make its system more resilient to

11        wildfire, consistent with the proposals in its 2024 Wildfire Mitigation Plan

12        submitted to the Commission in Case No. 22-00154-UT. As SPS witness Paul

13        McGregor describes, SPS is investing in four key areas: situational awareness,

14        system resiliency, operational mitigations, and customer support. These

15        investments will allow SPS to monitor its system more effectively and precisely

16        through advanced technologies, to conduct more frequent system repairs and

17        replacement and vegetation management activities in high wildfire risk areas, and

                                                19
                                      Case No. 25-00___-UT
                                       Direct Testimony
                                               of
                                      Adrian J. Rodriguez

 1        to communicate with its infrastructure and customers. These strategic investments,

 2        and related O&M expenses, are expected to benefit all SPS customers by allowing

 3        SPS to avoid system outages where possible, safely and promptly restoring power

 4        when an outage occurs, and helping ensure public safety by reducing the risk of a

 5        utility asset being the ignition source of a wildfire.

 6   Q.   Is keeping customer bills as low as possible a part of SPS’s priority to deliver

 7        excellent service to its customers?

 8   A.   Absolutely. We respect and appreciate the financial challenges that our customers

 9        are facing, and while increases to electric rates can present challenges for some

10        customers, the changes reflected in this case are needed so we can continue to

11        provide the safe, reliable energy on which they rely each day—at home and work.

12        Moreover, at a time when our customers are facing increased costs in many areas

13        of their household and business budgets, SPS is committed to keeping overall bill

14        changes as low as possible. While SPS must seek a base rate revenue increase to

15        make the investments and to do the work necessary to modernize its system to

16        provide the essential service its customers require, we remain focused on mitigating

17        costs for income-qualified New Mexico residential customers. We are therefore

18        proposing an Energy Assistance Program to support our customers in need of
                                                20
                                    Case No. 25-00___-UT
                                     Direct Testimony
                                             of
                                    Adrian J. Rodriguez

1         assistance.

 2   Q.   What program is SPS developing to assist income-qualified residential

 3        customers with their electric bills?

 4   A.   In order to help mitigate the impact of the rate increase on income-qualified New

5         Mexico residential customers, and consistent with New Mexico Statutes section 62-

6         8-6(C), SPS is proposing a new Electric Affordability Program that is designed to

7         provide assistance to households that have a high energy burden and the lowest

8         incomes. SPS is proposing that this program would assist qualifying customers by

9         paying a portion of their energy bills beyond what the Low Income Home Energy

10        Assistance Program provides. Ms. Lees provides an overview and the legislative

11        basis for this program. SPS witness Taylor Hurt explains the proposed criteria for

12        SPS customers to qualify for the program, along with the benefits of this program

13        for New Mexico customers and SPS’s proposal for funding the program.

14   Q.   Has SPS made efforts to control its cost of service?

15   A.   Yes. SPS works hard to control its operating costs while continuing to provide safe

16        and reliable service, and we have a number of processes and procedures in place to

17        ensure SPS’s costs are properly managed and remain at reasonable levels. SPS’s

18        operations witnesses discuss SPS’s processes and efforts to manage costs.
                                              21
                                     Case No. 25-00___-UT
                                      Direct Testimony
                                              of
                                     Adrian J. Rodriguez

1    Q.   Have SPS’s investments related to the clean energy transition supported its

2         ability to keep customer bills low?

3    A.   Yes. SPS’s efforts to lead the clean energy transition support its goal of keeping

4         overall bill increases at or below the rate of inflation, especially in times of high

 5        and unpredictable fuel costs. While some critics of renewable energy contend that

 6        the goals of environmental progress and affordable rates are inherently at odds,

 7        SPS’s past results have shown that electric utilities can decrease their carbon output
